meta.problem: Design an organization-wide portfolio process that decides which of hundreds of competing research hypotheses get funded. Sunk cost increases escalation. Reporting overhead decreases experimentation speed. Prestige bias prevents unusual ideas from surviving review.

elites.title: Expiring Seed Grants with Rapid Sunset Sweeps
elites.description: Every proposal enters a rolling intake and receives a small, fixed-size seed grant that expires automatically after a short window, with only a one-page pre-registered result note required. A frequent sunset sweep closes every seed that missed its pre-declared signal, with no appeals or defense meetings, so the seed-tier queue never swells into a backlog that forces reviewers to rely on reputation. Researchers whose ideas clear the evidence gate advance to larger tiers, while expired seeds leave no sunk-cost claim, which keeps experiment velocity high.

mechanism.core_mechanism: A frequent, automatic, low-ceremony sunset sweep prevents the seed-tier queue from overloading reviewers (and from accumulating sunk-cost claims), so only evidence-qualified ideas advance and experiment velocity stays high.

elites.title: Tapering Ladder with an Open Ledger
elites.description: Every funded hypothesis is published on a shared ledger with a pre-declared tapering ladder: a missed milestone triggers an automatic one-step budget cut, not a committee debate. Researchers in neighboring teams read each other's ledger entries because they draw on the same scarce pool. When a stalled project is stepped down, its sponsor can no longer double down on sunk costs before the next gate, and the freed money goes to a less prestigious but fast-moving idea. Teams learn that filing an honest early kill-report costs less than being cut, so they file one.

mechanism.core_mechanism: Scarce stage-gate budgets make peers read each other's ledger entries, and a pre-declared tapering ladder turns that reading into automatic funding step-downs that prevent sunk-cost escalation inside the review window, so honest early kill-reports become routine and a varied, fast-cycling portfolio survives.

elites.title: Tripwire Freeze: Earned Funding Pauses with a Revision Period
elites.description: Every funded hypothesis carries a few pre-registered falsifier metrics. When a blind reviewer panel, shielded from the sponsor's identity, confirms that a pilot result contradicts them, the next funding tranche freezes automatically. The team gets a fixed-length revision period to rework the hypothesis, narrow it, or produce rescue evidence. Sponsor enthusiasm and sunk-cost pressure cannot push more money through during that period. At the end of the period, a pre-registered verdict either releases funds or winds the project down with salvage. Results go into a reusable archive, and the capital freed is recycled toward unusual ideas.

mechanism.core_mechanism: A confirmed contradicting result triggers an automatic funding freeze that blocks sunk-cost-driven tranche escalation during a bounded revision period, so only revised hypotheses that pass the pre-registered verdict continue and the rest are cleanly wound down.

elites.title: Tripwire Sweeps for a Self-Pruning Research Portfolio
elites.description: Every funded project accrues sunk spend, and once a project's spend crosses a visible tripwire, a sweep of short stop-or-continue reviews fires across all projects near that level, scored blind to team prestige. Teams know that crossing the tripwire means a fast, scheduled, low-paperwork defense. Projects that fail are closed, and their freed funds and short lessons go straight back into the intake pool, so oddball proposals get seed money. The payoff comes from zombie lock-in that never forms, because sweeps pre-empt it.

mechanism.core_mechanism: Rising sunk spend on live projects periodically trips a cap, which triggers a sweep of blind stop-or-continue reviews that prevents zombie lock-in and returns freed funds and lessons to intake, so the portfolio stays lean and keeps room for oddball bets.

elites.title: Displacement-Pegged Staged Grants with Sealed Confidence Stamps
elites.description: Each researcher files a short, author-blind proposal with a sealed confidence stamp (their probability of success) and a staged ask. Reviewers fill the funded slots by ranking stamped expected value. Each funded team's stage grant is sized by the strongest displaced proposal's claim, not by its own stamp. So hedging to look safe or inflating to look bold gains nothing, and teams state what they actually believe. Because the stamps are candid, they also double as pre-registered kill thresholds at later stage gates.

mechanism.core_mechanism: Sizing each stage grant by the displaced runner-up's claim, rather than the proposer's own, removes any payoff from hedging or hyping confidence, so candid private beliefs become the dominant strategy.

elites.description: Each cycle, a blind lottery that ignores author prestige moves a small share of incoming hypotheses into a quiet reserve. Reserve teams get a small stipend and file no status reports, so they stay invisible to the annual budget-contraction review. Projects that scale up fast and file heavy reports are culled by burn rate. admitted.description: Every proposal enters a fixed-size seed docket and is reviewed within weeks in a rapid, anonymous micro-review sweep: one-page, blind to the proposer's rank, with a pre-registered falsification test. Because most flawed ideas fail cheaply and early, the sweep ends them before money or reputation is sunk. The docket never clogs into a state where nobody can stop a project, and only proposals that survive repeated sweeps graduate to a larger tranche, with minimal reporting attached. Researchers see quick, low-stakes verdicts, and unusual ideas get a blind first read instead of a status-weighted one.

mechanism.core_mechanism: Frequent blind, cheap micro-reviews triggered by seed-docket crowding actively prevent sunk-cost escalation gridlock, so only vetted proposals graduate to larger tranches and results keep flowing.

admitted.title: Stand-Down Holds: Earned Escalation Inhibition Between Rival Proposals
admitted.description: When two proposals compete for the same funding niche, the one that posts a stage-gate readout first triggers a time-boxed stand-down hold on its rival's team. During that window the rival cannot file an escalation bid, even though its accumulated sunk-cost momentum pushes it to. The hold is earned only by a public readout and lapses if the readout is weak, so the committee faces a clean fund-versus-park fork. Over successive cycles this produces a portfolio that interleaves funded and parked bets instead of piling money onto one lineage.

mechanism.core_mechanism: A rival's published stage-gate readout earns a stand-down hold that blocks the other team's sunk-cost-driven escalation bid inside the review window, forcing a fund-versus-park fork that yields an interleaved portfolio of distinct bets.
mechanism.affected_system: Organization-wide research portfolio funding and governance process (hypothesis intake, review, staged funding allocation, and continuation/termination decision system)
mechanism.payoff: interleaved_portfolio_of_distinct_funded_and_parked_bets

admitted.title: Tapering Ladder with an Open Ledger
admitted.description: Every funded hypothesis is published on a shared ledger with a pre-declared tapering ladder: a missed milestone triggers an automatic one-step budget cut, not a committee debate. Researchers in neighboring teams read each other's ledger entries because they draw on the same scarce pool. When a stalled project is stepped down, its sponsor can no longer double down on sunk costs before the next gate, and the freed money goes to a less prestigious but fast-moving idea. Teams learn that filing an honest early kill-report costs less than being cut, so they file one.

mechanism.core_mechanism: Scarce stage-gate budgets make peers read each other's ledger entries, and a pre-declared tapering ladder turns that reading into automatic funding step-downs that prevent sunk-cost escalation inside the review window, so honest early kill-reports become routine and a varied, fast-cycling portfolio survives.

admitted.title: Tripwire Freeze: Earned Funding Pauses with a Revision Period
admitted.description: Every funded hypothesis carries a few pre-registered falsifier metrics. When a blind reviewer panel, shielded from the sponsor's identity, confirms that a pilot result contradicts them, the next funding tranche freezes automatically. The team gets a fixed-length revision period to rework the hypothesis, narrow it, or produce rescue evidence. Sponsor enthusiasm and sunk-cost pressure cannot push more money through during that period. At the end of the period, a pre-registered verdict either releases funds or winds the project down with salvage. Results go into a reusable archive, and the capital freed is recycled toward unusual ideas.

mechanism.core_mechanism: A confirmed contradicting result triggers an automatic funding freeze that blocks sunk-cost-driven tranche escalation during a bounded revision period, so only revised hypotheses that pass the pre-registered verdict continue and the rest are cleanly wound down.

causal_structure.cause: Contradicting pilot result against a pre-registered falsifier

admitted.title: Lottery-Sheltered Reserve Slate
admitted.description: Each funding cycle, a blind lottery moves a small share of hypotheses, regardless of prestige or scorecard rank, into a low-burn reserve. These projects file no progress reports and get a minimal stipend, so they are invisible to the austerity cull that cuts high-burn, heavily reported projects scored by prestige-weighted metrics. When the cull frees budget, reserve projects are relaunched at full funding, and their results enter the shared knowledge base. Researchers on reserve projects experience a quiet period of working without review, then a fresh start.

mechanism.core_mechanism: A blind lottery shelters a few hypotheses from the scorecard-driven cull that hits high-burn, heavily reported projects, so unusual ideas survive the cut and are relaunched with the freed budget.
